TL;DR: the hour before bed matters more than total screen time. In a 2025 study of 1,200 kids aged 6 to 9, screen use in the last 60 minutes meant falling asleep about 19 minutes later, mostly with handheld devices, because of light, stimulating games and lost wind-down routines. What worked: a fixed screens-off time an hour before bed every night including weekends, devices charging in the kitchen, TV only in a shared room, and a choice of two books, and sleep onset normalised within two weeks. The author's point is that it's about when, not whether. Action: Nothing more unless you want a one-line reply for Hannah's group chat.
